newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank employees protest over bonuses.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank employees protest over bonuses.

text.p: About 1,000 employees of state-owned Krung Thai Bank protested in front of their Bangkok headquarters on Wednesday demanding bigger year-end bonuses.
A union spokesman told reporters the staff wanted a total year-end bonus payment of 5-1/2 months but management had refused to accept their demand.
Bank officials were unavailable for comment and details of any management counter-offer were unavailable. Negotiations between management and staff had broken down, the union spokesman said.
Krung Thai Bank is majority-owned by the finance ministry and a Bank of Thailand fund.
"The bank management refused to accept our demands because they fear that other state agencies will also make similar demands," the spokesman said.
Some of the protesters said they would continue their protests through the night until their demand was met while some others said they might strike on Thursday.
The protest follows the torching on Tuesday of Sanyo Universal Electric's warehouse and office building by employees angered by the management's refusal to pay them higher year-end bonuses.
Police were hunting a group of about 20 employees who were believed to have started the blaze.
Thai premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Wednesday that the action taken by Sanyo employees could scare away foreign investors.
